# Codex Sift

> Model router for the OpenAI Codex CLI. Routes each user turn to the cheapest model lane that should handle it.

Codex Sift was built by Roman Meclazcke. It is MIT licensed.

Sift sits in front of Codex as a local `model_provider`. On every user turn it asks TypeSafe Jev for typed signals (task_kind, difficulty, needs_reasoning, needs_planning, high_stakes, cross_cutting). Your `policy.yaml` maps those signals to flash, craft or forge. Only `model` and `reasoning.effort` are rewritten; the Codex TUI, sessions, tools and sandbox stay native.

## Hard facts

- Twelve live Jev prompts in `reports/e2e-routing.md`
- Estimated quota 7.5 vs always-forge baseline 16.2 (53.7% saved)
- Policy expectation match 11/12
- Average Jev latency 418 ms in that run
- Fail-open lane when Jev is down: craft (configurable)

## Who it is for

Developers who use the OpenAI Codex CLI and do not want every turn billed on the strongest model.

## Who it is not for

It is Codex-only. It is not an MCP server and does not patch `~/.codex/config.toml`.
